significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) law: language-ID decodability is U-shaped across depth, its trough coincides with peak shared-content decodability and cross-lingual intervention success, and a “deeper/wider trough” predicts better transfer. This fixes expectations for intervention efficacy and transfer from a measurable layerwise profile, rather than merely asserting that shared representations exist; Wendler et al., “Do Llamas Work in English?” (ACL 2024), and Müller et al., “First Align, then Predict” (2021) illustrate why the location and ordering of multilingual alignment and generation computations bear on current mechanistic explanations. It establishes both a phenomenon and a proposed shared-computation mechanism; verified false would distinctly rule out the claimed unified lifecycle and trough-based account, although it would not by itself select a replacement mechanism. The topic-substitution check lowers the assessment from the highest bands: generic shared-versus-language-specific layering is an obvious topic-level hypothesis, but the quoted predictive couplings involving “peak” patching success and “deeper/wider trough -> better transfer” add enough specific constraint to merit an above-median score.

reach.justification: The named handles are “trough layer and depth” and the “principled target layer for cross-lingual interventions,” together with the proposed predictor that “deeper/wider trough -> better transfer.” These are partly ex ante: once a model’s profile is extracted, the trough can forecast where editing or patching should work and potentially screen transfer quality before undertaking downstream cross-lingual use, rather than only explaining an observed failure. After per-model recalibration, the conclusion would still predict the transferable relations—maximum intervention success at the trough and transfer increasing with trough depth or width—but the asserted scope is clearest across model sizes, not across architectures, training regimes, or language-distance classes, so uptake is primarily by multilingual-model researchers and builders. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the broad topic alone supplies no trough metric or forecast, while these specific handles justify reach above the topic median but not the broad 9–10 band.
